chunks: Abu Ahmad al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Rahman al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abu Salamah narrated to us, saying: I read to Abu Umar al-San'ani from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
There is many a beggar with unkempt hair, covered in dust, wearing two tattered garments, who is turned away from the doors. If he swears by Allah, the Mighty and High, He will grant his oath.

key_terms.أَغْبَرَ: Covered in dust or pale from lack of food

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the beggar whose oath Allah fulfills?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Saduq, illustrates the concept of 'Istijaba' (divine responsiveness) where the intense faith of a humble, often overlooked servant—described as disheveled with matted hair—holds such weight that their oath compels God to fulfill it. In Shia scholarship, this highlights the spiritual potency of the 'Abid' (devotee) whose sincerity transcends social status, reinforcing the idea that God’s promise is bound by the truthfulness of the believer's invocation.
